items.text: رَبِّ اجْعَلْنِي مُقِيمَ الصَّلَاةِ وَمِن ذُرِّيَّتِي ۚ رَبَّنَا وَتَقَبَّلْ دُعَاءِ
رَبَّنَا هَبْ لَنَا مِنْ أَزْوَاجِنَا وَذُرِّيَّاتِنَا قُرَّةَ أَعْيُنٍ وَاجْعَلْنَا لِلْمُتَّقِينَ إِمَاماً
رَبِّ أَوْزِعْنِي أَنْ أَشْكُرَ نِعْمَتَكَ الَّتِي أَنْعَمْتَ عَلَيَّ وَعَلَىٰ وَالِدَيَّ وَأَنْ أَعْمَلَ صَالِحاً تَرْضَاهُ وَأَصْلِحْ لِي فِي ذُرِّيَّتِي
رَبَّنَا آتِنَا فِي الدُّنْيَا حَسَنَةً وَفِي الْآخِرَةِ حَسَنَةً وَقِنَا عَذَابَ النَّارِ
وَاعْبُدُوا اللَّهَ وَلَا تُشْرِكُوا بِهِ شَيْئاً ۖ وَبِالْوَالِدَيْنِ إِحْسَاناً
يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا قُوا أَنفُسَكُمْ وَأَهْلِيكُمْ نَاراً
وَاللَّهُ جَعَلَ لَكُم مِّنْ أَنفُسِكُمْ أَزْوَاجاً وَجَعَلَ لَكُم مِّن أَزْوَاجِكُم بَنِينَ وَحَفَدَةً
وَبِالْوَالِدَيْنِ إِحْسَاناً ۚ إِمَّا يَبْلُغَنَّ عِندَكَ الْكِبَرَ أَحَدُهُمَا أَوْ كِلَاهُمَا فَلَا تَقُل لَّهُمَا أُفٍّ وَلَا تَنْهَرْهُمَا
وَاخْفِضْ لَهُمَا جَنَاحَ الذُّلِّ مِنَ الرَّحْمَةِ وَقُل رَّبِّ ارْحَمْهُمَا كَمَا رَبَّيَانِي صَغِيراً
وَوَصَّيْنَا الْإِنسَانَ بِوَالِدَيْهِ حَمَلَتْهُ أُمُّهُ وَهْناً عَلَىٰ وَهْنٍ وَفِصَالُهُ فِي عَامَيْنِ أَنِ اشْكُرْ لِي وَلِوَالِدَيْكَ
وَإِذْ قَالَ لُقْمَانُ لِابْنِهِ وَهُوَ يَعِظُهُ يَا بُنَيَّ لَا تُشْرِكْ بِاللَّهِ ۖ إِنَّ الشِّرْكَ لَظُلْمٌ عَظِيمٌ
يَا بُنَيَّ أَقِمِ الصَّلَاةَ وَأْمُرْ بِالْمَعْرُوفِ وَانْهَ عَنِ الْمُنكَرِ وَاصْبِرْ عَلَىٰ مَا أَصَابَكَ
وَلَا تُصَعِّرْ خَدَّكَ لِلنَّاسِ وَلَا تَمْشِ فِي الْأَرْضِ مَرَحاً ۖ إِنَّ اللَّهَ لَا يُحِبُّ كُلَّ مُخْتَالٍ فَخُورٍ
وَاقْصِدْ فِي مَشْيِكَ وَاغْضُضْ مِن صَوْتِكَ ۚ إِنَّ أَنكَرَ الْأَصْوَاتِ لَصَوْتُ الْحَمِيرِ
الْمَالُ وَالْبَنُونَ زِينَةُ الْحَيَاةِ الدُّنْيَا ۖ وَالْبَاقِيَاتُ الصَّالِحَاتُ خَيْرٌ عِندَ رَبِّكَ ثَوَاباً وَخَيْرٌ أَمَلاً
وَأْمُرْ أَهْلَكَ بِالصَّلَاةِ وَاصْطَبِرْ عَلَيْهَا ۖ لَا نَسْأَلُكَ رِزْقاً ۖ نَّحْنُ نَرْزُقُكَ
إِنَّمَا أَمْوَالُكُمْ وَأَوْلَادُكُمْ فِتْنَةٌ ۚ وَاللَّهُ عِندَهُ أَجْرٌ عَظِيمٌ
يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا اتَّقُوا اللَّهَ وَقُولُوا قَوْلاً سَدِيداً
يُصْلِحْ لَكُمْ أَعْمَالَكُمْ وَيَغْفِرْ لَكُمْ ذُنُوبَكُمْ ۗ وَمَن يُطِعِ اللَّهَ وَرَسُولَهُ فَقَدْ فَازَ فَوْزاً عَظِيماً
إِنَّ اللَّهَ يَأْمُرُ بِالْعَدْلِ وَالْإِحْسَانِ وَإِيتَاءِ ذِي الْقُرْبَىٰ
وَلَا تَسْتَوِي الْحَسَنَةُ وَلَا السَّيِّئَةُ ۚ ادْفَعْ بِالَّتِي هِيَ أَحْسَنُ
فَإِذَا الَّذِي بَيْنَكَ وَبَيْنَهُ عَدَاوَةٌ كَأَنَّهُ وَلِيٌّ حَمِيمٌ
وَمَا يُلَقَّاهَا إِلَّا الَّذِينَ صَبَرُوا وَمَا يُلَقَّاهَا إِلَّا ذُو حَظٍّ عَظِيمٍ
وَسَارِعُوا إِلَىٰ مَغْفِرَةٍ مِّن رَّبِّكُمْ وَجَنَّةٍ عَرْضُهَا السَّمَاوَاتُ وَالْأَرْضُ أُعِدَّتْ لِلْمُتَّقِينَ
الَّذِينَ يُنفِقُونَ فِي السَّرَّاءِ وَالضَّرَّاءِ وَالْكَاظِمِينَ الْغَيْظَ وَالْعَافِينَ عَنِ النَّاسِ ۗ وَاللَّهُ يُحِبُّ الْمُحْسِنِينَ
فَبِمَا رَحْمَةٍ مِّنَ اللَّهِ لِنتَ لَهُمْ ۖ وَلَوْ كُنتَ فَظّاً غَلِيظَ الْقَلْبِ لَانفَضُّوا مِنْ حَوْلِكَ
فَاعْفُ عَنْهُمْ وَاسْتَغْفِرْ لَهُمْ وَشَاوِرْهُمْ فِي الْأَمْرِ
فَإِذَا عَزَمْتَ فَتَوَكَّلْ عَلَى اللَّهِ ۚ إِنَّ اللَّهَ يُحِبُّ الْمُتَوَكِّلِينَ
يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا اصْبِرُوا وَصَابِرُوا وَرَابِطُوا وَاتَّقُوا اللَّهَ لَعَلَّكُمْ تُفْلِحُونَ
إِنَّ مَعَ الْعُسْرِ يُسْراً
فَإِذَا فَرَغْتَ فَانصَبْ * وَإِلَىٰ رَبِّكَ فَارْغَب
وَقُل رَّبِّ زِدْنِي عِلْماً
إِنَّ اللَّهَ مَعَ الصَّابِرِينَ
وَبَشِّرِ الصَّابِرِينَ * الَّذِينَ إِذَا أَصَابَتْهُم مُّصِيبَةٌ قَالُوا إِنَّا لِلَّهِ وَإِنَّا إِلَيْهِ رَاجِعُونَ
أُولَٰئِكَ عَلَيْهِمْ صَلَوَاتٌ مِّن رَّبِّهِمْ وَرَحْمَةٌ ۖ وَأُولَٰئِكَ هُمُ الْمُهْتَدُونَ
وَإِذَا سَأَلَكَ عِبَادِي عَنِّي فَإِنِّي قَرِيبٌ ۖ أُجِيبُ دَعْوَةَ الدَّاعِ إِذَا دَعَانِ
وَلَا تَنسَوُا الْفَضْلَ بَيْنَكُمْ ۚ إِنَّ اللَّهَ بِمَا تَعْمَلُونَ بَصِيرٌ
اللَّهُ لَا إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا هُوَ الْحَيُّ الْقَيُّومُ
مَّن ذَا الَّذِي يُقْرِضُ اللَّهَ قَرْضاً حَسَناً فَيُضَاعِفَهُ لَهُ أَضْعَافاً كَثِيرَةً
آَمَنَ الرَّسُولُ بِمَا أُنْزِلَ إِلَيْهِ مِنْ رَبِّهِ وَالْمُؤْمِنُونَ
لَا يُكَلِّفُ اللَّهُ نَفْساً إِلَّا وُسْعَهَا
رَبَّنَا لَا تُؤَاخِذْنَا إِنْ نَسِينَا أَوْ أَخْطَأْنَا
رَبَّنَا وَلَا تَحْمِلْ عَلَيْنَا إِصْراً كَمَا حَمَلْتَهُ عَلَى الَّذِينَ مِنْ قَبْلِنَا
رَبَّنَا وَلَا تُحَمِّلْنَا مَا لَا طَاقَةَ لَنَا بِهِ ۖ وَاعْفُ عَنَّا وَاغْفِرْ لَنَا وَارْحَمْنَا
إِنَّ رَبِّي لَطِيفٌ لِّمَا يَشَاءُ ۚ إِنَّهُ هُوَ الْعَلِيمُ الْحَكِيمُ
قَالَ إِنَّمَا أَشْكُو بَثِّي وَحُزْنِي إِلَى اللَّهِ
إِنَّهُ مَن يَتَّقِ وَيَصْبِرْ فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ لَا يُضِيعُ أَجْرَ الْمُحْسِنِينَ
رَبِّ هَبْ لِي مِنَ الصَّالِحِينَ
فَبَشَّرْنَاهُ بِغُلَامٍ حَلِيمٍ
قَالَ يَا بُنَيَّ إِنِّي أَرَىٰ فِي الْمَنَامِ أَنِّي أَذْبَحُكَ فَانظُرْ مَاذَا تَرَىٰ
قَالَ يَا أَبَتِ افْعَلْ مَا تُؤْمَرُ ۖ سَتَجِدُنِي إِن شَاءَ اللَّهُ مِنَ الصَّابِرِينَ
إِنَّ هَٰذَا لَهُوَ الْبَلَاءُ الْمُبِينُ * وَفَدَيْنَاهُ بِذِبْحٍ عَظِيمٍ
وَسَلَامٌ عَلَيْهِ يَوْمَ وُلِدَ وَيَوْمَ يَمُوتُ وَيَوْمَ يُبْعَثُ حَيّاً
يَا يَحْيَىٰ خُذِ الْكِتَابَ بِقُوَّةٍ ۖ وَآتَيْنَاهُ الْحُكْمَ صَبِيّاً
وَبَرّاً بِوَالِدَيْهِ وَلَمْ يَكُن جَبَّاراً عَصِيّاً
قَالَ إِنِّي عَبْدُ اللَّهِ آتَانِيَ الْكِتَابَ وَجَعَلَنِي نَبِيّاً
وَجَعَلَنِي مُبَارَكاً أَيْنَ مَا كُنتُ وَأَوْصَانِي بِالصَّلَاةِ وَالزَّكَاةِ مَا دُمْتُ حَيّاً
وَبَرّاً بِوَالِدَتِي وَلَمْ يَجْعَلْنِي جَبَّاراً شَقِيّاً
وَالسَّلَامُ عَلَيَّ يَوْمَ وُلِدتُّ وَيَوْمَ أَمُوتُ وَيَوْمَ أُبْعَثُ حَيّاً
وَكَانَ يَأْمُرُ أَهْلَهُ بِالصَّلَاةِ وَالزَّكَاةِ وَكَانَ عِندَ رَبِّهِ مَرْضِيّاً
فَقُولَا لَهُ قَوْلاً لَّيِّناً لَّعَلَّهُ يَتَذَكَّرُ أَوْ يَخْشَىٰ
قَالَ رَبِّ اشْرَحْ لِي صَدْرِي * وَيَسِّرْ لِي أَمْرِي * وَاحْلُلْ عُقْدَةً مِّن لِّسَانِي * يَفْقَهُوا قَوْلِي
وَاجْعَل لِّي وَزِيراً مِّنْ أَهْلِي
كَيْ نُسَبِّحَكَ كَثِيراً * وَنَذْكُرَكَ كَثِيراً * إِنَّكَ كُنتَ بِنَا بَصِيراً
وَأَلْقَيْتُ عَلَيْكَ مَحَبَّةً مِّنِّي وَلِتُصْنَعَ عَلَىٰ عَيْنِي
إِذْ تَمْشِي أُخْتُكَ فَتَقُولُ هَلْ أَدُلُّكُمْ عَلَىٰ مَن يَكْفُلُهُ ۖ فَرَجَعْنَاكَ إِلَىٰ أُمِّكَ كَيْ تَقَرَّ عَيْنُهَا وَلَا تَحْزَنَ
إِنَّ السَّمْعَ وَالْبَصَرَ وَالْفُؤَادَ كُلُّ أُولَٰئِكَ كَانَ عَنْهُ مَسْئُولاً
وَلَا تَقْفُ مَا لَيْسَ لَكَ بِهِ عِلْمٌ
وَقُل لِّعِبَادِي يَقُولُوا الَّتِي هِيَ أَحْسَنُ ۚ إِنَّ الشَّيْطَانَ يَنزَغُ بَيْنَهُمْ
رَبُّكُمْ أَعْلَمُ بِمَا فِي نُفُوسِكُمْ ۚ إِن تَكُونُوا صَالِحِينَ فَإِنَّهُ كَانَ لِلْأَوَّابِينَ غَفُوراً
وَآتِ ذَا الْقُرْبَىٰ حَقَّهُ وَالْمِسْكِينَ وَابْنَ السَّبِيلِ وَلَا تُبَذِّرْ تَبْذِيراً
وَإِمَّا تُعْرِضَنَّ عَنْهُمُ ابْتِغَاءَ رَحْمَةٍ مِّن رَّبِّكَ تَرْجُوهَا فَقُل لَّهُمْ قَوْلاً مَّيْسُوراً
وَلَا تَجْعَلْ يَدَكَ مَغْلُولَةً إِلَىٰ عُنُقِكَ وَلَا تَبْسُطْهَا كُلَّ الْبَسْطِ فَتَقْعُدَ مَلُوماً مَّحْسُوراً
وَالَّذِينَ إِذَا أَنفَقُوا لَمْ يُسْرِفُوا وَلَمْ يَقْتُرُوا وَكَانَ بَيْنَ ذَٰلِكَ قَوَاماً
وَالَّذِينَ لَا يَشْهَدُونَ الزُّورَ وَإِذَا مَرُّوا بِاللَّغْوِ مَرُّوا كِرَاماً
وَالَّذِينَ إِذَا ذُكِّرُوا بِآيَاتِ رَبِّهِمْ لَمْ يَخِرُّوا عَلَيْهَا صُمّاً وَعُمْيَاناً
أَلَا بِذِكْرِ اللَّهِ تَطْمَئِنُّ الْقُلُوبُ
إِنَّ اللَّهَ لَا يُغَيِّرُ مَا بِقَوْمٍ حَتَّىٰ يُغَيِّرُوا مَا بِأَنفُسِهِمْ
مَنْ عَمِلَ صَالِحاً مِّن ذَكَرٍ أَوْ أُنثَىٰ وَهُوَ مُؤْمِنٌ فَلَنُحْيِيَنَّهُ حَيَاةً طَيِّبَةً
ادْعُ إِلَىٰ سَبِيلِ رَبِّكَ بِالْحِكْمَةِ وَالْمَوْعِظَةِ الْحَسَنَةِ ۖ وَجَادِلْهُم بِالَّتِي هِيَ أَحْسَنُ
وَاصْبِرْ وَمَا صَبْرُكَ إِلَّا بِاللَّهِ ۚ وَلَا تَحْزَنْ عَلَيْهِمْ وَلَا تَكُ فِي ضَيْقٍ مِّمَّا يَمْكُرُونَ
إِنَّ اللَّهَ مَعَ الَّذِينَ اتَّقَوا وَّالَّذِينَ هُم مُّحْسِنُونَ
يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا اسْتَجِيبُوا لِلَّهِ وَلِلرَّسُولِ إِذَا دَعَاكُمْ لِمَا يُحْيِيكُمْ
وَاتَّقُوا فِتْنَةً لَّا تُصِيبَنَّ الَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوا مِنكُمْ خَاصَّةً ۖ وَاعْلَمُوا أَنَّ اللَّهَ شَدِيدُ الْعِقَابِ
فَابْتَغُوا عِندَ اللَّهِ الرِّزْقَ وَاعْبُدُوهُ وَاشْكُرُوا لَهُ
وَقُلْ رَبِّ أَدْخِلْنِي مُدْخَلَ صِدْقٍ وَأَخْرِجْنِي مُخْرَجَ صِدْقٍ
وَاجْعَل لِّي مِن لَّدُنكَ سُلْطَاناً نَّصِيراً
وَقُلْ جَاءَ الْحَقُّ وَزَهَقَ الْبَاطِلُ ۚ إِنَّ الْبَاطِلَ كَانَ زَهُوقاً
وَنُنَزِّلُ مِنَ الْقُرْآنِ مَا هُوَ شِفَاءٌ وَرَحْمَةٌ لِّلْمُؤْمِنِينَ
قُلْ كُلٌّ يَعْمَلُ عَلَىٰ شَاكِلَتِهِ فَرَبُّكُمْ أَعْلَمُ بِمَنْ هُوَ أَهْدَىٰ سَبِيلاً
وَسَبِّحْ بِحَمْدِ رَبِّكَ قَبْلَ طُلُوعِ الشَّمْسِ وَقَبْلَ غُرُوبِهَا
وَمِنْ آنَاءِ اللَّيْلِ فَسَبِّحْ وَأَطْرَافَ النَّهَارِ لَعَلَّكَ تَرْضَىٰ
وَلَا تَمُدَّنَّ عَيْنَيْكَ إِلَىٰ مَا مَتَّعْنَا بِهِ أَزْوَاجاً مِّنْهُمْ زَهْرَةَ الْحَيَاةِ الدُّنْيَا
وَرِزْقُ رَبِّكَ خَيْرٌ وَأَبْقَىٰ
إِنَّ اللَّهَ وَمَلَائِكَتَهُ يُصَلُّونَ عَلَى النَّبِيِّ ۚ يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا صَلُّوا عَلَيْهِ وَسَلِّمُوا تَسْلِيماً
يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا اذْكُرُوا اللَّهَ ذِكْراً كَثِيراً
وَسَبِّحُوهُ بُكْرَةً وَأَصِيلاً
هُوَ الَّذِي يُصَلِّي عَلَيْكُمْ وَمَلَائِكَتُهُ لِيُخْرِجَكُم مِّنَ الظُّلُمَاتِ إِلَى النُّورِ
يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا اتَّقُوا اللَّهَ وَلْتَنظُرْ نَفْسٌ مَّا قَدَّمَتْ لِغَدٍ
وَلَا تَكُونُوا كَالَّذِينَ نَسُوا اللَّهَ فَأَنسَاهُمْ أَنفُسَهُمْ
لَوْ أَنزَلْنَا هَٰذَا الْقُرْآنَ عَلَىٰ جَبَلٍ لَّرَأَيْتَهُ خَاشِعاً مَُّتَصَدِّعاً مِّنْ خَشْيَةِ اللَّهِ
وَتِلْكَ الْأَمْثَالُ نَضْرِبُهَا لِلنَّاسِ لَعَلَّهُمْ يَتَفَكَّرُونَ
هُوَ اللَّهُ الَّذِي لَا إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا هُوَ ۖ عَالِمُ الْغَيْبِ وَالشَّهَادَةِ ۖ هُوَ الرَّحْمَٰنُ الرَّحِيمُ
فَاصْبِرْ صَبْراً جَمِيلاً
إِنَّهُمْ يَرَوْنَهُ بَعِيداً * وَنَرَاهُ قَرِيباً
فَاسْتَقِمْ كَمَا أُمِرْتَ وَمَن تَابَ مَعَكَ وَلَا تَطْغَوْا
وَأَقِمِ الصَّلَاةَ طَرَفَيِ النَّهَارِ وَزُلَفاً مِّنَ اللَّيْلِ ۚ إِنَّ الْحَسَنَاتِ يُذْهِبْنَ السَّيِّئَاتِ
وَاصْبِرْ فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ لَا يُضِيعُ أَجْرَ الْمُحْسِنِينَ
وَلِلَّهِ غَيْبُ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ وَإِلَيْهِ يُرْجَعُ الْأَمْرُ كُلُّهُ فَاعْبُدْهُ وَتَوَكَّلْ عَلَيْهِ
إِنَّ الدِّينَ عِندَ اللَّهِ الْإِسْلَامُ
قُلْ إِن كُنتُمْ تُحِبُّونَ اللَّهَ فَاتَّبِعُونِي يُحْبِبْكُمُ اللَّهُ وَيَغْفِرْ لَكُمْ ذُنُوبَكُمْ
وَاللَّهُ غَفُورٌ رَّحِيمٌ
فَتَقَبَّلَهَا رَبُّهَا بِقَبُولٍ حَسَنٍ وَأَنبَتَهَا نَبَاتاً حَسَناً
هُنَالِكَ دَعَا زَكَرِيَّا رَبَّهُ ۖ قَالَ رَبِّ هَبْ لِي مِن لَّدُنكَ ذُرِّيَّةً طَيِّبَةً ۖ إِنَّكَ سَمِيعُ الدُّعَاءِ
فَنَادَتْهُ الْمَلَائِكَةُ وَهُوَ قَائِمٌ يُصَلِّي فِي الْمِحْرَابِ أَنَّ اللَّهَ يُبَشِّرُكَ بِيَحْيَىٰ
مُصَدِّقاً بِكَلِمَةٍ مِّنَ اللَّهِ وَسَيِّداً وَحَصُوراً وَنَبِيّاً مِّنَ الصَّالِحِينَ
يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا اذْكُرُوا اللَّهَ ذِكْراً كَثِيراً * وَسَبِّحُوهُ بُكْرَةً وَأَصِيلاً
وَقُل رَّبِّ اغْفِرْ وَارْحَمْ وَأَنتَ خَيْرُ الرَّاحِمِينَ
وَقُل رَّبِّ أَعُوذُ بِكَ مِنْ هَمَزَاتِ الشَّيَاطِينِ * وَأَعُوذُ بِكَ رَبِّ أَن يَحْضُرُونِ
رَبَّنَا اصْرِفْ عَنَّا عَذَابَ جَهَنَّمَ ۖ إِنَّ عَذَابَهَا كَانَ غَرَاماً
رَبِّ اشْرَحْ لِي صَدْرِي * وَيَسِّرْ لِي أَمْرِي
إِنَّ مَعِيَ رَبِّي سَيَهْدِينِ
وَإِذَا مَرِضْتُ فَهُوَ يَشْفِينِ
وَالَّذِي هُوَ يُطْعِمُنِي وَيَسْقِينِ
رَبِّ هَبْ لِي حُكْماً وَأَلْحِقْنِي بِالصَّالِحِينَ
وَاجْعَل لِّي لِسَانَ صِدْقٍ فِي الْآخِرِينَ
وَاجْعَلْنِي مِن وَرَثَةِ جَنَّةِ النَّعِيمِ
وَلَا تُخْزِنِي يَوْمَ يُبْعَثُونَ * يَوْمَ لَا يَنفَعُ مَالٌ وَلَا بَنُونَ * إِلَّا مَنْ أَتَى اللَّهَ بِقَلْبٍ سَلِيمٍ
فَتَبَسَّمَ ضَاحِكاً مِّن قَوْلِهَا وَقَالَ رَبِّ أَوْزِعْنِي أَنْ أَشْكُرَ نِعْمَتَكَ الَّتِي أَنْعَمْتَ عَلَيَّ
وَأَنْ أَعْمَلَ صَالِحاً تَرْضَاهُ وَأَدْخِلْنِي بِرَحْمَتِكَ فِي عِبَادِكَ الصَّالِحِينَ
قَالَ هَٰذَا مِن فَضْلِ رَبِّي لِيَبْلُوَنِي أَأَشْكُرُ أَمْ أَكْفُرُ
وَمَن شَكَرَ فَإِنَّمَا يَشْكُرُ لِنَفْسِهِ ۖ وَمَن كَفَرَ فَإِنَّ رَبِّي غَنِيٌّ كَرِيمٌ
قَالَ رَبِّ إِنِّي ظَلَمْتُ نَفْسِي فَاغْفِرْ لِي فَغَفَرَ لَهُ
رَبِّ إِنِّي لِمَا أَنزَلْتَ إِلَيَّ مِنْ خَيْرٍ فَقِيرٌ
فَجَاءَتْهُ إِحْدَاهُمَا تَمْشِي عَلَى اسْتِحْيَاءٍ
إِنَّ خَيْرَ مَنِ اسْتَأْجَرْتَ الْقَوِيُّ الْأَمِينُ
وَالَّذِينَ جَاهَدُوا فِينَا لَنَهْدِيَنَّهُمْ سُبُلَنَا ۚ وَإِنَّ اللَّهَ لَمَعَ الْمُحْسِنِينَ
فَسُبْحَانَ اللَّهِ حِينَ تُمْسُونَ وَحِينَ تُصْبِحُونَ
وَلَهُ الْحَمْدُ فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ وَعَشِيّاً وَحِينَ تُظْهِرُونَ
وَمِنْ آيَاتِهِ أَنْ خَلَقَ لَكُم مِّنْ أَنفُسِكُمْ أَزْوَاجاً لِّتَسْكُنُوا إِلَيْهَا وَجَعَلَ بَيْنَكُم مَّوَدَّةً وَرَحْمَةً
فَأَقِمْ وَجْهَكَ لِلدِّينِ حَنِيفاً ۚ فِطْرَتَ اللَّهِ الَّتِي فَطَرَ النَّاسَ عَلَيْهَا
لا تَبْدِيلَ لِخَلْقِ اللَّهِ ۚ ذَٰلِكَ الدِّينُ الْقَيِّمُ وَلَٰكِنَّ أَكْثَرَ النَّاسِ لَا يَعْلَمُونَ
Start your day by smiling at your children: a smile is charity, and a home takes its shape from the first moment of the morning.
items.source: Parenting guidance — drawn from the hadith «تبسمك في وجه أخيك صدقة»

items.text: Before you criticise, put your hand on your child's head and lower your voice: «الرفق لا يكون في شيء إلا زانه» — gentleness adorns whatever it touches.
items.source: Parenting guidance — drawn from the hadith on gentleness

items.text: Set aside ten minutes a day to listen to your child without interrupting — it tells them they are safe and respected.
Do not compare your children to each other or to anyone else's; being fair between them starts with seeing each one as themselves.
Teach your child one du'a this week and say it together: whoever takes a path in search of knowledge is walking a path to Paradise.
items.source: Parenting guidance — drawn from the hadith on knowledge

items.text: Mark the smallest achievement with a kind word: praise that names the effort builds a confident child who loves doing good.
When your child angers you, take a breath before you answer: «الصبر عند الصدمة الأولى» — patience counts at the first shock.
items.source: Parenting guidance — drawn from the hadith on patience

items.text: Read your child the story of a prophet or a companion each night before sleep: hearts grow around the people they are shown.
Do not let worship disappear from the house; praying in congregation with your children — even two rak'ahs — teaches more than a thousand lectures.
Forgive yourself for your parenting mistakes and ask Allah to guide you: a parent is a shepherd, and a shepherd sometimes errs and then puts it right.
items.source: Parenting guidance — drawn from the hadith of the shepherd

items.text: Replace “don't do that” with “what if we did this instead?” — pointing somewhere is what earns you a response.
When your child does wrong, separate the child from the behaviour: you are dear to us, and this particular thing was wrong.
Give your child a small corner of the house for reading and quiet — a visible invitation to settle.
Accept your child's apology at once, and teach them to repair what they broke rather than simply be punished for it.
When your child speaks, come down to their eye level and put down whatever is in your hands — there is no higher respect.
Get your children used to saying “thank you” and “جزاك الله خيرًا” for any help around the house.
Take your child to the mosque gently and cheerfully, and teach them stillness through love rather than fear.
Make Friday feel different at home: good scent, and Surat al-Kahf read together.
Bring your children into cooking or setting the table — working together is where responsibility grows.
When you shop, teach your child the difference between a real need and a passing want.
Keep a small jar at home called “the good jar”, where your child puts whatever they like for those in need.
Do not shout at a crying child. Say instead: I am here with you, and when you are calm we will talk.
Hug your children several times a day: being held is what safety feels like before a child has words for it.
Listen to your child's small stories with real attention, so that they trust you with the large ones later.
Promise your child nothing you cannot deliver: keeping your word is the ground their sense of safety stands on.
Teach your child how to say “no” to a stranger, or to anything that makes them uncomfortable.
Set screen and phone hours for the house, and be the first to keep to them.
Keep the dinner table completely free of phones: mealtime is the family's talking time.
Praise the attempt and the effort spent, not only the cleverness or the result: “I am proud of how hard you worked.”
Teach your children to settle their small disagreements by talking and taking turns.
When your child is angry, help them put the feeling into words: “I can see that this upset you.”
Say the morning and evening adhkar out loud at home, so your children learn them simply by hearing them again and again.
Hold a fifteen-minute family sitting each week on one simple point of faith or character.
Encourage your children into a sport that serves them — swimming or running — so the body is built well.
Do not discuss your child's faults in front of relatives or friends: their dignity is a trust you are holding.
If you find out your child did wrong, take it up with them alone in the room — not in front of their brothers and sisters.
Teach your child that asking permission before entering a room is an adab the Qur'an taught, and it protects everyone's privacy.
Train your child to keep the household's business inside the house.
Let your child choose their own clothes, within reason, so they learn to decide and to stand on their own.
Teach your children never to mock anyone for their looks, their colour or their clothes: «إن الله لا ينظر إلى صوركم» — Allah does not look at your forms.
items.source: Parenting guidance — drawn from the hadith «إن الله لا ينظر إلى صوركم»

items.text: Thank your wife in front of the children, and thank your husband in front of them: how the two of you treat each other is what they copy.
When you travel or go out, bring the children into the planning and let them choose some of it.
Put up a simple daily chart and let your child tick off a prayer or a piece of homework once it is done.

Teach your child istighfar and the du'a of Yunus in distress: «لَا إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا أَنتَ سُبْحَانَكَ إِنِّي كُنتُ مِنَ الظَّالِمِينَ». Its meaning: there is no god but You, glory be to You, I have been among the wrongdoers.
items.source: Parenting guidance — the wording is Qur'an, Surat al-Anbiya' 21:87

items.text: When you see your child helping anyone at all, thank them on the spot: “how beautiful your hands are when they help.”
Teach your son that manhood is in gentleness and in protecting the weak — not in force or in shouting.
Teach your daughter modesty, and pride in who she is and in the character her faith gives her.
Explain the reason behind a rule simply, instead of handing down a bare order.
Be patient with your child's endless questions: curiosity is the engine of every bit of learning they will do.
If you do not know the answer to your child's question about faith or science, say so honestly: “good question — let's go and find out together.”
Teach your child the du'a for entering and leaving the bathroom, so adab reaches even the smallest corner of their day.
Teach your child the du'a for travelling, and to look for barakah in every journey.
Keep a small library at home with illustrated stories of the prophets.
Encourage your child to read by leaving a book beside their bed every night.
At meals, get your child used to never criticising food: if they want it they eat it, and if not they leave it politely.
Teach your child not to waste water in wudu or in the shower: looking after a blessing is how you thank Allah for it.
Train your child to switch off lights and devices nobody is using — a small, daily sense of responsibility.
When visiting relatives, teach your children a warm greeting, asking permission, and how to sit with people.
If your child is afraid of something, never make light of the fear — hold them and make them feel safe.
Teach your child to honour a trust: a toy borrowed from a friend goes back whole and clean.
Get your children used to telling the truth and owning a mistake without fearing what follows.
Make bedtime a warm moment: a hand on the head, the last two surahs, and a du'a for good.
If your child had a hard day at school, listen first and be the safe place they come back to.
Teach your child that failing is not the end of the world — it is another go at learning something.
Let your child try things and discover under your eye, without tying their hands entirely.
Teach your children to respect the elderly and to help them carry what is heavy.
Get your children used to kindness towards animals and never harming them: «في كل كبد رطبة أجر» — there is reward in every living creature.
items.source: Parenting guidance — drawn from the hadith «في كل كبد رطبة أجر»

items.text: When your child plants something, remind them that everyone who benefits from it later is written for them.
Teach your child to respect their teachers, to listen politely, and to remember what they owe them.
Keep a small signal or a password between you and your children — a quick, private way to reach each other.
Do not step into every detail of your children's play unless there is danger: let them negotiate it out.
Teach your child that apologising is strength, not weakness, and that what makes it possible is humility.
Let your home be one where Allah's name is said often — in tasbih, in praise, in du'a.
Get your child used to keeping promises and appointments: a Muslim who promises, delivers.
Teach your children to compete in doing good, without bitterness or envy.
If you see a gift in your child — drawing, calligraphy, memorising Qur'an — feed it and cheer it on.
Have your children make du'a for your parents, their grandparents, for mercy and health — that is how lasting birr is planted.
Teach your child never to pry or to steal a look into what belongs to someone else.
When there is trouble between your children, hear each one alone and without taking a side, before you judge.
Teach your child that digital honesty is knowing Allah sees them on the internet and on the phone as everywhere else.
Steer your child towards content that is useful and right for their age, so the hours are not simply spent.
Explain to your child that games and phones are a small amusement, not the whole of life.
Teach your children to visit their cousins on both sides — this is how the ties of kinship are kept strong.
Let your children help choose and wrap the Eid gifts, and spread the joy with you.
Teach your child salat al-istikhara for when they are torn between two good options.
Get your children used to saying bismillah before drinking, thanking Allah after, and drinking in three breaths.
Teach your child not to talk with food in their mouth — for their safety as much as for good manners.
When your child looks sad, ask: “would you like me to listen, or would you like a hug?”
Teach your child that a beautiful character leaves a deeper mark on people than expensive clothes ever do.
Get your children used to the dhikr for leaving the house: «بِسْمِ اللَّهِ تَوَكَّلْتُ عَلَى اللَّهِ» — in the name of Allah, I place my trust in Allah.
Teach your children to say bismillah and to praise Allah when they put on new clothes.
Keep a box at home for recycling paper or saving leftover food — responsibility learned by doing.
Teach your child to lay out their day between prayer, schoolwork, play and sleep.
Thank your child when they do what you asked the first time: praise is what makes it happen again.
If your child is struggling with a subject, help them through it in small encouraging steps and without tension.
Teach your child that swallowing anger and forgiving a friend is something Allah raises them for.
Get your children used to giving salam out loud when they come into the house.
Teach your child that Allah sees in the dark as He sees in the light: knowing you are seen is where uprightness begins.
Let your child feel that their home is the safest, most loving place in the world.
Remember that du'a made for your children when they are not there works wonders: never tire of making it.
Teach your child that hardship is an opening for patience and for drawing nearer to Allah — not anger from Him.
Tell your child, again and again, that your love does not depend on their performance or their marks.
Teach your child to make du'a for themselves, for their parents and for the Muslims after every prayer.
Build good memories with your children in every season and every Eid.
Be the support your child always turns to, so they never go looking for it among strangers.
Teach your child to hold to their faith, their values and their character with confidence and love.
Remember that your children read what you do and where you stand far more closely than they listen to your advice.
And last: ask Allah every day for guidance, for tawfiq, and for barakah in your children.
Give your child a moment to think before sleep, and ask: “what was the best thing that happened today, and what made you happy?”
Teach your children to respect privacy and never to open someone else's messages or devices without asking.
If your child is worked up or angry, give them a cushion or a squeeze toy to let the charge out safely.
Teach your children to seek refuge in Allah from the shaytan when anger stirs.
Keep a daily family hour with no screens or phones at all, so people actually talk to each other.
If you promised your child a reward for finishing something, give it the moment they finish.
Train your child to pack their own school bag and lay out their clothes each evening before bed.
Teach your child the du'a for sleep: «بِاسْمِكَ اللَّهُمَّ أَمُوتُ وَأَحْيَا» — in Your name, O Allah, I die and I live — and reassure them that Allah is guarding them while they sleep.
Keep a chart at home that rotates the small chores between the children — fairness and responsibility in one place.
Thank your child warmly, and in front of everyone, when they go and help a friend or a neighbour.
If your child mispronounces a word or an ayah, correct it calmly and kindly, and never laugh at them.
Teach your child that truth always brings you out, and that lying cuts the rope of trust and safety.
Train your children to switch the devices off and get ready for bed an hour early, so the mind can settle.
If your child has a hard project or assignment, break it down with them into small, encouraging steps.
Teach your child that their body is their own, and that nobody may touch them in a way that makes them uncomfortable.
Before sleep, take your child's hand, read the bedtime adhkar together, and name the good things they did today.

مَنْ لاَ يَرْحَمُ لاَ يُرْحَمُ

إِنَّ اللَّهَ رَفِيقٌ يُحِبُّ الرِّفْقَ فِي الأَمْرِ كُلِّهِ
لا يُؤْمِنُ أَحَدُكُمْ حَتَّى يُحِبَّ لأَخِيهِ مَا يُحِبُّ لِنَفْسِهِ
مَنْ كَانَ يُؤْمِنُ بِاللَّهِ وَالْيَوْمِ الآخِرِ فَلْيَقُلْ خَيْرًا أَوْ لِيَصْمُتْ

الدِّينُ النَّصِيحَةُ
لاَ تَغْضَبْ
الْمُسْلِمُ مَنْ سَلِمَ الْمُسْلِمُونَ مِنْ لِسَانِهِ وَيَدِهِ
مَنْ عَالَ جَارِيَتَيْنِ حَتَّى تَبْلُغَا جَاءَ يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ أَنَا وَهُوَ
السَّاعِي عَلَى الأَرْمَلَةِ وَالْمِسْكِينِ كَالْمُجَاهِدِ فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ، أَوِ الْقَائِمِ اللَّيْلَ الصَّائِمِ النَّهَارَ
بَلِّغُوا عَنِّي وَلَوْ آيَةً
اللَّهُمَّ مَنْ وَلِيَ مِنْ أَمْرِ أُمَّتِي شَيْئًا فَشَقَّ عَلَيْهِمْ فَاشْقُقْ عَلَيْهِ وَمَنْ وَلِيَ مِنْ أَمْرِ أُمَّتِي شَيْئًا فَرَفَقَ بِهِمْ فَارْفُقْ بِهِ
